_comment: The DM-32UV Kraken image: patch manifests applied in order, each built on the previous one's output.
Paths are relative to /w inside the dm32uv-re Docker image. tools/build.sh mounts this repo at /w/dm32uv-unleashed
and the dm32uv-re checkout at /w/dm32/dm32uv-re, whatever the folders are called on the host.
tools/build_image.py reads this file. Add a patch by appending to 'patches' (and its claims file to
name: kraken

test._note: Phase B (booted, gdb) times out about 1 run in 3 on the mi_rng-only image too: emulator timing, not a patch fault. One retry.

patches.id: kraken_ui (P3 F1 F2 F4 F6 P5)

exclude_claims.name: ramdump_probe_code
exclude_claims.why: dm32uv-re's live-RAM-capture probe handler (sector 0x030e1000) is not in this image: image.json patches are mi_rng and kraken_ui only, neither of which calls or writes it, and stock has 0xFF there. kraken_ui5_code (F3 DMR link) takes the sector (2026-10-30). Its SRAM claim ramdump_cursor stays reserved and untouched.

exclude_claims.name: mi_rng_tap_buf
exclude_claims.why: measurement-build-only claim (mi_rng_tap.patch.json); the production mi_rng in this image never touches 0x18005000-0x18007000. Our SRAM claims kraken_ui_state2/feat_state/ui3_state/bigbuf reuse that range (2026-10-29).

exclude_claims.name: snake_code
exclude_claims.why: dm32uv-re's Snake example is not in this image and cannot be: it edits the same eleven menu sites as kraken_ui (P3 replaced it). Its sectors 0x030e8000-0x030ea000 are erased in our image; F13's blob kraken_ui4 uses them (2026-10-29).

exclude_claims.name: snake_state
exclude_claims.why: Snake's SRAM (see snake_code); unused in this image. kraken_ui4_state takes 0x18007000-0x18007400 (2026-10-29).
